blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your computer connects to the internet and communicates with other devices? Let's explore the foundational models and protocols that make this possible.

blocks.markdown: Computer networks are essential for enabling communication between devices. To manage this complexity, we use layered models like the OSI and TCP/IP models. These models help standardize how data is transmitted across networks.

blocks.title: OSI Model
blocks.text: The OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model is a conceptual framework used to understand network interactions in seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application.

blocks.title: TCP/IP Model
blocks.text: The TCP/IP model is a more practical framework with four layers: Link, Internet, Transport, and Application. It is the foundation of the internet.

blocks.caption: Comparison of OSI and TCP/IP Models

blocks.markdown: The OSI model is primarily used for teaching and understanding, while the TCP/IP model is used in real-world networking. Each layer in these models has specific functions and protocols.

blocks.title: Understanding IP Addresses
blocks.prompt: Explain the structure of an IPv4 address and its purpose.

steps.text: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit number that uniquely identifies a device on a network.
It is typically represented in decimal format as four octets separated by periods, e.g., 192.168.1.1.
Each octet can range from 0 to 255, allowing for over 4 billion unique addresses.

blocks.answer: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit number, represented as four decimal octets, used to identify devices on a network.

blocks.title: IP Addresses and Ports
blocks.text: IP addresses identify devices, while ports identify specific applications or services on those devices.

blocks.title: TCP vs. UDP
blocks.prompt: Compare TCP and UDP in terms of reliability and use cases.

steps.text: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is connection-oriented, ensuring reliable data transfer with error checking and correction.
UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless, offering faster data transfer without reliability guarantees.
TCP is used for applications where reliability is crucial, such as web browsing and email.
UDP is used for applications where speed is more important than reliability, such as video streaming and online gaming.

blocks.answer: TCP is reliable and used for critical data transfer, while UDP is faster and used for applications where speed is prioritized over reliability.

blocks.markdown: A simple request/response on the web involves a client sending a request to a server, which processes the request and sends back a response. This interaction typically uses the HTTP protocol over TCP.

points: The OSI and TCP/IP models provide frameworks for understanding network communication.
IP addresses and ports are crucial for identifying devices and services on a network.
TCP and UDP are key transport layer protocols with different reliability and speed characteristics.
